## Summary

Add opt-in FlashInfer SSD prefill for Mamba2 with
`--mamba-prefill-backend flashinfer` (default remains `triton`). This accelerates
recurrent prefill while preserving live states and reusable checkpoints.

## Implementation

- Prepare packed-sequence/checkpoint metadata once per forward. Capture selected
  checkpoints in the same scan, without changing checkpoint policy.
- Isolate padding in a discarded sequence so it cannot alter real final states.

Code: [SSD adapter](https://github.com/NVShreyas/sglang/blob/313fcd4ff8/python/sglang/kernels/ops/mamba/flashinfer_ssd.py),
[correctness tests](https://github.com/NVShreyas/sglang/blob/313fcd4ff8/test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_flashinfer_ssd_prefill.py).
Currently requires SM100 and static contiguous pools; unified/page-major pools
are unsupported.

## Dependency / release blocker

**Waiting for a FlashInfer release containing the validated SSD changes before
updating the dependency pin and completing standalone qualification.**

SGLang main currently pins FlashInfer **0.7.1**. That version already exposes
the SSD/checkpoint APIs, but its numerical implementation differs from the one
validated here:

- 0.7.1 stores processed delta in **BF16** and uses shape-dependent scan dispatch.
- Upstream [FlashInfer #6051](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6051)
  changes processed delta to **FP16** and consolidates dispatch into an
  **exact-only scan** family. It also retires the prefix route with its documented
  overflow/NaN issue.

Our validation used unmodified upstream
[`461037fbf`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/461037fbf52227e6343ccbc9fc977337c1bf672b),
reporting `0.7.2+g461037fbf`: this is a **development/source build**, not a
qualified released wheel. This is a numerical-qualification dependency, not a
claim that the APIs are absent or cannot run in 0.7.1.

Once a release includes these changes, update the SGLang dependency pin and rerun
standalone SSD kernel correctness and full GSM8K **with and without SSD** on the
same environment. Those standalone accuracy runs remain pending.

## AgentX results

Model: [NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super 120B A12B NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4),
revision `ff433f5493e25d631c9f12b5d55c674229923d02`; one B200, TP1 per variant.
Both configurations use the same instrumented SGLang base (main `41cbe65de0`)
and upstream FlashInfer `461037fbf` build. ReplaySSM is enabled in both;
only the recurrent-prefill backend changes (Triton w/o SSD, FlashInfer w/ SSD).

### Public trace and replay settings

- AIPerf AgentX MVP, pinned dataset
  [`semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126-256k`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126-256k),
  alias `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k`; all eligible sessions, seed42.
- **900 measured seconds per point**, one run; concurrency counts **session
  trees** including subagents, not in-flight requests. Preserve recorded turn
  delays, trajectory-start ratios0–1 and global idle-gap cap10s.
- Flush cache before each point; retain AgentX trajectory warmup into measurement
  and use `first_turn_prefix` cache-busting. No extra session cap.
- FP8 KV, FP16 state, EAGLE three steps/four positions, **synthetic AL3.2527**
  (`match-expected`, fixed-token mode). Context1,048,576; prefill/chunk32768;
  page64; `extra_buffer`, tracking128; stochastic rounding/Philox5;
  memory fraction0.85; max-running256; graph cap256; `trtllm_mha`.
  No offloading/unified pools. AIPerf commit `754356e9a39acc6cc6afb242d123bb57c3fb6f75`.

| Session trees | w/o SSD (output tok/s) | w/ SSD (output tok/s) | SSD gain |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 358.63 | 358.63 | 0.0% |
| 32 | 906.82 | 960.78 | +6.0% |
| 64 | 1,216.77 | **1,393.49** | **+14.5%** |

## Validation and remaining work

- Standalone rebase: 25 CPU metadata-layout cases, 5 invalid-input checks,
  3 selected kernel-namespace tests, lazy registry/capability checks, Python syntax
  and CI test-registration checks passed. The numerical adapter, GPU tests and
  microbenchmark are unchanged from the qualified PR version.
- GPU numerical and end-to-end validation on the rebased standalone branch
  remain to be run; the previous combined-build results are not rebase validation.

- On the previously qualified build: passed 6 SSD adapter tests and 7 numerical
  cases, with unchanged numerical tolerances.
- On the previously qualified build: passed 10 real-acceptance requests covering chunked prefill, packed inputs
  and checkpoint restoration; synthetic acceptance was disabled for these checks.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

`flashinfer_ssd_prefill` does not pass `out` to `ssd_combined_fwd`, so every call copies the whole output back here. When the token count is not a multiple of 128, it also copies x, dt, B, C, and `initial_states` to add the padding sequence (lines 150-160). At FlashInfer 461037fbf, the Cake path accepts any positive length (it handles a partial last chunk itself) and writes a contiguous token-major `out` directly.

**Example**

With 32768 tokens and 128 heads, this copy alone reads and writes 512 MiB per Mamba layer on every prefill.

**Fix**

Once the pin requires 461037fbf, pass `out=out` and drop the padding sequence and `pad_tokens`.

+128-token physical extent; a tail is padded as a separate, discarded sequence
+so it cannot decay a real request's final state. Checkpoint positions are
+exclusive sequence-relative endpoints supplied by the caller's tracking policy.

+import torch

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SSDPrefillMetadata:
+    num_tokens: int
+    num_sequences: int
+    padding: int
+    seq_idx: torch.Tensor
+    chunk_indices: torch.Tensor
+    chunk_offsets: torch.Tensor
+    seq_chunk_cumsum: torch.Tensor

+            raise ValueError("Checkpoint extends past its sequence")

+    num_tokens = sum(lengths)
+    padding = -num_tokens % 128
+    packed_lengths = lengths + ([padding] if padding else [])
+    seq_ids, chunks, offsets, cumulative = [], [], [], [0]
+    endpoints = []
+    initial_rows = []
+    start = 0

+            checkpoint_lengths[row]
+            if checkpoint_lengths is not None and row < len(lengths)

+        pad_tokens(dt),
+        A,
+        pad_tokens(B),
+        pad_tokens(C),
+        D=D.to(torch.bfloat16) if D is not None else None,
+        dt_bias=dt_bias,
+        dt_softplus=True,
+        # Upstream Cake SSD uses exact scan with FP16 processed delta. Keep

+"""Packed Mamba2 prefill adapter for FlashInfer's checkpoint-capable SSD.
+
+Metadata is built once per forward, not once per layer. FlashInfer requires a
+128-token physical extent; a tail is padded as a separate, discarded sequence
+so it cannot decay a real request's final state. Checkpoint positions are
+exclusive sequence-relative endpoints supplied by the caller's tracking policy.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SSDPrefillMetadata:
+    num_tokens: int
+    num_sequences: int
+    padding: int
+    seq_idx: torch.Tensor
+    chunk_indices: torch.Tensor
+    chunk_offsets: torch.Tensor
+    seq_chunk_cumsum: torch.Tensor
+    checkpoint_token_indices: torch.Tensor | None
+    checkpoint_state_slots: torch.Tensor | None
+    initial_checkpoint_rows: torch.Tensor | None
+    initial_checkpoint_slots: torch.Tensor | None
+
+
+def prepare_ssd_prefill_metadata(
+    lengths: list[int],
+    device: torch.device,
+    checkpoint_lengths: list[int] | None = None,
+    checkpoint_slots: list[int] | torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> SSDPrefillMetadata:
+    """Build packed logical chunks from CPU lengths, without a GPU readback."""
+    if not lengths or any(length <= 0 for length in lengths):
+        raise ValueError("SSD prefill requires nonempty positive sequence lengths")
+    if (checkpoint_lengths is None) != (checkpoint_slots is None):
+        raise ValueError("Checkpoint lengths and slots must be supplied together")
+    if checkpoint_lengths is not None:
+        if len(checkpoint_lengths) != len(lengths) or len(checkpoint_slots) != len(
+            lengths
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Expected one checkpoint length and slot per sequence")
+        if any(end > length for end, length in zip(checkpoint_lengths, lengths)):
+            raise ValueError("Checkpoint extends past its sequence")
+
+    num_tokens = sum(lengths)
+    padding = -num_tokens % 128
+    packed_lengths = lengths + ([padding] if padding else [])
+    seq_ids, chunks, offsets, cumulative = [], [], [], [0]
+    endpoints = []
+    initial_rows = []
+    start = 0
+    for row, length in enumerate(packed_lengths):
+        seq_ids.extend([row] * length)
+        end = (
+            checkpoint_lengths[row]
+            if checkpoint_lengths is not None and row < len(lengths)
+            else -1
+        )
+        checkpoint = start + end if end >= 0 else -1
+        # Native capture happens only at logical-segment ends. Split an
+        # interior checkpoint into two segments of the SAME sequence, so
+        # state carries through without resetting or launching a second scan.
+        # An inactive row must have endpoint -1. Physical slot IDs may remain
+        # on device; never synchronize just to inspect a destination.
+        if end == 0:
+            initial_rows.append(row)
+        cursor = start
+        while cursor < start + length:
+            chunks.append(cursor // 128)
+            offsets.append(cursor % 128)
+            next_cursor = min((cursor // 128 + 1) * 128, start + length)
+            if cursor < checkpoint < next_cursor:
+                next_cursor = checkpoint
+            cursor = next_cursor
+        cumulative.append(len(chunks))
+        if checkpoint_lengths is not None:
+            endpoints.append(checkpoint if end > 0 else -1)
+        start += length
+
+    def tensor(values):
+        return torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+    slots = None
+    if checkpoint_slots is not None:
+        slots = (
+            checkpoint_slots.to(device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+            if isinstance(checkpoint_slots, torch.Tensor)
+            else tensor(checkpoint_slots)
+        )
+        if padding:
+            slots = torch.cat((slots, slots.new_full((1,), -1)))
+    initial_rows_tensor = torch.tensor(initial_rows, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
+    return SSDPrefillMetadata(
+        num_tokens=num_tokens,
+        num_sequences=len(lengths),
+        padding=padding,
+        seq_idx=tensor(seq_ids).unsqueeze(0),
+        chunk_indices=tensor(chunks),
+        chunk_offsets=tensor(offsets),
+        seq_chunk_cumsum=tensor(cumulative),
+        checkpoint_token_indices=tensor(endpoints)
+        if checkpoint_lengths is not None
+        else None,
+        checkpoint_state_slots=slots,
+        initial_checkpoint_rows=initial_rows_tensor if initial_rows else None,
+        initial_checkpoint_slots=slots.index_select(0, initial_rows_tensor).long()
+        if initial_rows
+        else None,
+    )
+
+
+def flashinfer_ssd_prefill(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    dt: torch.Tensor,
+    A: torch.Tensor,
+    B: torch.Tensor,
+    C: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    D: torch.Tensor | None,
+    dt_bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+    initial_states: torch.Tensor,
+    metadata: SSDPrefillMetadata,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    checkpoint_states: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Write token-major output/checkpoints and return real-sequence final states.
+
+    Inputs follow ``ssd_combined_fwd``: x [1,T,H,64], B/C [1,T,G,128],
+    initial states [N,H,64,128]. Caller masks cold initial states to zero. The
+    checkpoint pool must be contiguous, with distinct destination slots. This
+    adapter intentionally includes padding/output-copy costs in its benchmarks."""
+    from flashinfer.mamba import ssd_combined_fwd
+
+    if x.shape[0] != 1 or x.shape[1] != metadata.num_tokens:
+        raise ValueError("Input extent does not match packed SSD metadata")
+    if initial_states.shape[0] != metadata.num_sequences:
+        raise ValueError("Expected one initial state per real sequence")
+    if (checkpoint_states is None) != (metadata.checkpoint_token_indices is None):
+        raise ValueError("Checkpoint metadata and storage must be supplied together")
+    if metadata.initial_checkpoint_rows is not None:
+        checkpoint_states.index_copy_(
+            0,
+            metadata.initial_checkpoint_slots,
+            initial_states.index_select(0, metadata.initial_checkpoint_rows),
+        )
+
+    def pad_tokens(value):
+        if not metadata.padding:
+            return value
+        zeros = value.new_zeros((1, metadata.padding, *value.shape[2:]))
+        return torch.cat((value, zeros), dim=1)
+
+    if metadata.padding:
+        initial_states = torch.cat(
+            (initial_states, initial_states.new_zeros((1, *initial_states.shape[1:]))),
+            dim=0,
+        )
+    result, final_states = ssd_combined_fwd(
+        pad_tokens(x),
+        pad_tokens(dt),
+        A,
+        pad_tokens(B),
+        pad_tokens(C),
+        D=D.to(torch.bfloat16) if D is not None else None,
+        dt_bias=dt_bias,
+        dt_softplus=True,
+        # Upstream Cake SSD uses exact scan with FP16 processed delta. Keep
+        # normal nonnegative step sizes; no clamp-based dispatch workaround.
+        dt_limit=(0.0, float("inf")),
+        initial_states=initial_states,
+        seq_idx=metadata.seq_idx,
+        chunk_indices=metadata.chunk_indices,
+        chunk_offsets=metadata.chunk_offsets,
+        seq_chunk_cumsum=metadata.seq_chunk_cumsum,
+        checkpoint_token_indices=metadata.checkpoint_token_indices,
+        checkpoint_state_slots=metadata.checkpoint_state_slots,
+        checkpoint_states=checkpoint_states,
+        return_final_states=True,
+    )
+    out.copy_(result[:, : metadata.num_tokens])
+    return final_states[: metadata.num_sequences]

+"""Benchmark checkpoint-preserving packed SSD adapters, not just the main kernel."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+sys.path.insert(
+    0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "registered/kernels/ops/mamba")
+)
+from test_flashinfer_ssd_prefill import SSDCase, check_error
+
+
+def milliseconds(fn):
+    for _ in range(5):
+        fn()
+    begin, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(
+        enable_timing=True
+    )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    begin.record()
+    for _ in range(20):
+        fn()
+    end.record()
+    end.synchronize()
+    return begin.elapsed_time(end) / 20
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def scalar_uniform_final(case):
+    """Independent FP32 recurrence, batched across equal-length requests."""
+    length = case.lengths[0]
+    batch = len(case.lengths)
+    state = case.initial.float()
+    x = case.x.view(batch, length, case.heads, 64)
+    dt = case.dt.view(batch, length, case.heads)
+    B = case.B.reshape(batch, length, case.groups, 128)
+    for token in range(length):
+        delta = torch.nn.functional.softplus(dt[:, token].float() + case.bias)
+        projection = (
+            B[:, token].float().repeat_interleave(case.heads // case.groups, dim=1)
+        )
+        state = (
+            state * torch.exp(delta * case.A)[:, :, None, None]
+            + x[:, token].float()[:, :, :, None]
+            * (delta[:, :, None] * projection)[:, :, None, :]
+        )
+    return state
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()

+    import flashinfer
+
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            dict(
+                torch=torch.__version__,
+                flashinfer=flashinfer.__version__,
+                gpu=torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+            )
+        ),
+        flush=True,
+    )
+    for total, sequences in [
+        (4096, 1),
+        (4096, 16),
+        (16384, 16),
+        (32768, 16),
+        (32768, 64),
+    ]:
+        lengths = [total // sequences] * sequences

+
+        def triton():
+            _, final = case.reference(checkpoints=False)
+            case.pool[case.slot_tensor] = final
+            return final
+
+        final = case.run().clone()
+        checkpoints = case.pool[case.slot_tensor].clone()
+        ref_final = triton()
+        passed = True
+        for name, actual, expected in [
+            ("bench_output", case.out, case.ref_out),
+            ("bench_final", final, ref_final),
+            ("bench_checkpoint", checkpoints, final),
+        ]:
+            try:
